title: Velocity graphs and components
target: Read a velocity graph and describe motion in two directions.
criteria: Use signed velocity-time area to find displacement.
Represent horizontal and vertical components separately.
Distinguish graph height, slope and vector magnitude.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A velocity-time graph is constant at +3 m/s for 4 s. What is displacement?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A cart moves at −4 m/s for 2 s, then +2 m/s for 3 s. What is net displacement?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A drone’s velocity components are 7 m/s east and 2 m/s south. What is its general direction?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A velocity has components +6 m/s in x and −8 m/s in y. What is its magnitude?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: On a velocity-time graph, which feature represents acceleration?
cpa.guide: Slope is Δv/Δt; height is velocity and area is displacement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A horizontal v–t segment sits at −5 m/s. Which interpretation is correct?
options: Negative acceleration because the graph is below zero.
Zero velocity because the line is flat.
Constant negative velocity, zero acceleration, and negative displacement over positive elapsed time.
cpa.guide: Height, slope, and signed area describe different quantities.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
